title: Cytokine Feedback Loop
description: Interactive feedback-loop model of immune-to-brain signaling. Gut inflammation releases cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF) that signal the brain and its microglia, producing sleep problems, low mood, and fatigue; sleep problems and stress feed back into inflammation. Learners set gut inflammation, sleep hours, and stress, watch the loop strengthen, and break one link to see the whole loop weaken.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: neuroscience (gut-brain axis)
publisher: Gut Check: The Neuroscience of How Your Gut and Brain Talk
learningObjectives: Explain immune-to-brain signaling as a feedback loop in which gut inflammation releases cytokines that act on the brain and produce sleep problems, low mood, and fatigue.
Analyze how breaking one link in the loop (treating inflammation, protecting sleep, or managing stress) weakens the whole loop.
prerequisites: Inflammation as the body's response to infection or injury
Afferent vagus nerve signals carry information from the gut to the brain
keyQuestions: How do cytokines made in the gut change how the brain feels and acts?
What makes a feedback loop reinforcing?
Why does breaking any one link weaken the whole loop?
Why might someone still feel tired after gut inflammation is treated?
misconceptions: The brain is completely sealed off from the immune system.
Fatigue during illness is laziness or all in your head.
Inflammation is the only cause of low mood in people with gut disease.
